pr_title: *: track cluster-level analyze jobs and make it persistent
pr_body:

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and 
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close #32403

Problem Summary:
`show analyze status` only shows analyze jobs on self instance and the previous analyze jobs are cleared after rebooting.

### What is changed and how it works?

Previously analyze jobs are tracked in memory. In the PR we introduce a system table `mysql.analyze_jobs` and track analyze jobs in the system table. The implementation of `show analyze status` is changed to read recent 30 analyze jobs from `mysql.analyze_jobs`. In this way the analyze jobs are persistent even after rebooting TiDB. Besides, each TiDB server dumps analyze jobs into the same table so `show analyze status` shows cluster-level analyze jobs. We also introduce two more fields `instance` and `process_id` to indicate on which TiDB and which process the analyze job is executed.

issue_context.title: improve `show analyze status`
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement

Currently, `show analyze status` only shows recent 20 analyze jobs on self instance. Besides, once TiDB reboots, all the previous analyze jobs will be cleared. That brings some inconvenience:
1. users must log in the TiDB who is stats owner in order to check auto analyze jobs.
2. If OOM happens, TiDB reboots and we cannot get any information from `show analyze status` when we try to find out whether OOM is caused by analyze.

We wish: 
1. `show analyze status` shows cluster-level analyze jobs
2.  The analyze history is persistent.

review_comments: When will this happen? the last updating?
`delta == 0` means that `job.Delta.Count` doesn't reach threshold so we don't need to dump it. I forget to handle the last updating. Fix it by update `processed_rows` when calling `finishAnalyzeJob`.
Is this possible to directly use `func (s *session) LastInsertID() uint64`?

I am not sure about it. We use `session.GetSessionVars().StmtCtx.PrevLastInsertID` to evaluate `LAST_INSERT_ID()`.
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/7c69e74bd9dad30dc9d724dc9d0b3fc759973b40/expression/builtin_info.go#L358-L363
In `ResetContextOfStmt`, we set `StmtCtx.PrevLastInsertID` rather than `StmtCtx.LastInsertID`.
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/7c69e74bd9dad30dc9d724dc9d0b3fc759973b40/executor/executor.go#L1904-L1908
IMO, `(*session).LastInsertID` seems to be for the current statement rather than the previous statement.

Seems we plan to record the connection ID for `analyze` initiated by the client and record process ID for auto analyze.
I think the column name and the comment is a bit confusing.

The ID is the same as `ID` in `show processlist`(#31724 makes auto-analyze appear in `show processlist`). #31724 uses the fixed and reserved ID for auto analyze.
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/164bee7ae88ab5bb28ef6e6528bd6963f4fb7ba2/util/processinfo.go#L265-L274
And the ID is used to set `GetSessionVars().ConnectionID` of the internal session which is going to execute auto-analyze.
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/164bee7ae88ab5bb28ef6e6528bd6963f4fb7ba2/domain/domain.go#L1812-L1823
